interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymph node metastasis, and absence of lymphovascular invasion. The preoperative PSA was elevated at 8.1. The surgical pathology showed a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pT3a stage with extraprostatic extension. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA level and the T3a stage. The biopsy showed perineural invasion, which is a relevant finding. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. The current horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 54 months without an event. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trend is crucial for refining this assessment. The fixed estimated horizon is 53.08 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 42.46–63.70 months; its coverage has not been validated.
